title: Seamless tileable fBm noise textures
purpose: Generate gradient noise on a lattice that repeats every period cells, summed over octaves whose periods double, so one period of the field tiles without seams; sample it into Float32Array or RGBA8 grids and three.js repeat-wrapped DataTextures. Use it for terrain detail, clouds, stone, dissolve masks and shader noise.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: The noise functions need no three.js; createNoiseTexture takes three.js r152 or later as THREE (colorSpace); only 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: periodicGradientNoise
exports.summary: Gradient noise in [-1, 1] whose lattice repeats every period cells; zero at lattice points.

exports.name: fbmNoise
exports.summary: Octave sum with doubling frequency and lattice period, normalized to [-1, 1]; repeats every period.

exports.name: noiseField
exports.summary: One period sampled at texel centres; tiles in both directions.

exports.name: noiseTextureData
exports.summary: RGBA8 bytes: grey, or four independent fields with channels 'rgba'.

exports.name: latticeHash
exports.summary: 32-bit unsigned hash of a lattice point and a seed (Math.imul arithmetic).

exports.name: NOISE_DEFAULTS
exports.summary: Frozen default options: period 8, octaves 4, gain 0.5, seed 1, channels grey.

options.name: period
options.meaning: Lattice cells per tile along each axis at the base octave; more cells give finer features.

options.name: octaves
options.meaning: Layers of noise; each doubles the frequency and the lattice period.

options.name: seed
options.meaning: Selects the gradients; octave k uses seed + k.

options.name: channels
options.meaning: One field in RGB, or four independent fields.

limits: Classic gradient noise with eight gradient directions: it shows faint axis-aligned and diagonal structure and is not isotropic like simplex noise. The value range is [-1, 1] by construction but most values fall well inside it, so textures look mid-grey without contrast stretching. Periodicity is exact only for coordinates that are representable (texel centres of power-of-two sizes); elsewhere it holds within rounding. Computed on the CPU, about width * height * octaves noise evaluations, so large textures take time; there is no GPU version and no 3D or animated noise. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Gradient noise with a quintic fade on a wrapped integer lattice
